title: How to Read Tire Size Markings

calculator.title: Size marking mapping calculator
calculator.description: Choose any one marking and the other two will update automatically. Repeated names include the ETRTO value so different sizes stay clear.
calculator.note: The calculator includes common combinations with all three markings available. It explains the naming relationship and does not replace rim, frame-clearance, or manufacturer fitment checks.

standards.title: Start with the three common markings
standards.description: The same bicycle tire may show ETRTO/ISO, inch, and French markings at the same time. They are different ways to express one tire size, not three different tires. For rim compatibility, start with ETRTO and use the other markings to read packaging and sidewall information.
standards.readFirstDescription: 37-622 means an approximate 37 mm nominal width and a 622 mm bead seat diameter (BSD). The second number determines the rim diameter; “28 inch” or “700C” alone is not enough.

etrto.name: ETRTO / ISO marking
etrto.description: The format is width–bead seat diameter, with both values in millimetres. 37-622 means about 37 mm nominal width and a 622 mm BSD, which is the clearest reference for rim diameter.

inch.name: Inch / imperial marking
inch.description: A traditional format that usually gives approximate outer diameter × width. The same inch name can refer to different BSDs, so use it to read older tires or packaging and confirm the ETRTO before fitting.

french.name: French marking
french.description: Usually written as approximate outer diameter × width plus a letter code. In 700 × 35C, C is a rim-diameter code. It is common on road and gravel tires, but the letter does not replace the exact ETRTO/BSD.

comparison.title: Three ways to write the same tire size

availability.title: Common marking reference
availability.description: These entries are grouped by rim diameter for lookup and comparison. They are not a fitment result for a specific frame or bike. Before installation, use the tire sidewall ETRTO, rim specification, and manufacturer instructions.

mystery.title: Why 28 inch and 29 inch can both be 622
mystery.sameDescription: Both 28 inch touring or road tires and 29 inch MTB tires can use the same 622 mm BSD. Width, frame clearance, and the exact tire construction still determine whether a fit is safe.
mystery.contextBody: 28 inches is the traditional European size for touring bikes. 29 inches is a marketing term introduced in the US for voluminous MTB tires that have an approximate outer diameter of 29 inches when mounted.
mystery.realityBody: Both designations are imprecise. A narrow 28 inch road tire can be about 26 inches in outer diameter, while a wide 60 mm or larger MTB tire can be almost 30 inches.
